revision_notes: Original citation (eGA project page) did not actually mention passport or immigration and was too weak to support the score on its own. Fresher, more specific evidence found: a 2020 presidential decree (2020-244/PR/MI, Journal Officiel) established an inter-agency committee — ANSIE, the Immigration Directorate of the national police, national security, customs, civil aviation and justice — to pilot introduction of an API-PNR (advance passenger information) data-sharing system, and biometric passports with a digital archiving platform have been issued since 2017. This confirms a genuine, named government plan for cross-agency passport/immigration data-sharing, but there is no evidence the API-PNR system or passport database is technically connected to the X-Road/Caravan data exchange. Code 2 (Planned) confirmed, now on stronger sourcing than the original single citation.

Definition: Current operational status of the data exchange system
Comments: X-Road data exchange platform (called 'Caravan') implemented by e-Governance Academy and partners, completed end of 2021. Backend interoperability platform operational with PKI. ANSIE manages the platform. World Bank confirms: 'The government has rolled out a backend interoperability platform based on the open-source X-ROAD system developed in Estonia.' Fewer than 10 platforms are using it so far due to lack of mandatory connection law. ASYCUDAWorld customs system in place. Some services operational but adoption limited. Platform partially operational.
